findings.finding: Markedly impaired. Poor performance on set-shifting (Trail Making Test B), abstraction/similarities, and response inhibition; perseverative errors on Wisconsin-style sorting. Pattern consistent with dorsolateral and orbitofrontal dysfunction.
Reduced letter (phonemic) fluency out of proportion to category fluency — a frontal/executive signature rather than a semantic-store deficit.

Impaired emotion recognition (Ekman faces) and deficits on theory-of-mind / faux-pas tasks, with reduced affective empathy on the Interpersonal Reactivity Index — supports the bvFTD social-cognitive phenotype.
Relatively spared. Encoding and free recall reduced in a dysexecutive (retrieval) pattern, but recognition and cued recall are comparatively preserved.
Preserved. Copy of complex figure and clock contour intact; errors, when present, reflect poor planning rather than a perceptual or constructional deficit.
Fluent with intact single-word comprehension and confrontation naming largely preserved; no agrammatism or semantic loss — argues against a primary progressive aphasia variant.
Reduced insight (anosognosia), stimulus-bound responses, and reduced concern for test performance noted during the session.

Standardized behavioral inventory (e.g., FBI/CBI) shows prominent apathy and loss of empathy that the bedside MoCA underestimates — consistent with a behavioral syndrome out of proportion to the global cognitive score.

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile shows a predominant frontal-executive and social-cognition impairment with relative sparing of episodic memory (preserved recognition) and visuospatial/constructional function. The dissociation between impaired executive/social-cognitive performance and preserved memory and visuospatial domains points to selective dysfunction of anterior (frontal-network) cortices

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Exclude opportunistic CNS infections with CSF and HIV-specific markers given immunocompromised history.
Coordinate ART continuation and CNS-penetrant regimen review.
Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

differential.key_features: HIV well-controlled (undetectable VL 8 years); HAND can still occur but pattern is typically subcortical, not frontotemporal lobar.
MRI would show asymmetric T2 hyperintensities; CSF JCV PCR helps; not the pattern here.
Two failed antidepressant trials; imaging confirms neurodegeneration.
Acute / subacute opportunistic infection with focal mass-effect lesions; not the described pattern.

key_clinical_evidence: Well-controlled HIV with progressive lobar frontotemporal pattern is not HAND; HAND is typically subcortical.
Opportunistic infections must be excluded but are unlikely with sustained virologic control.
Failed antidepressant trials reinforce that this is a primary neurodegenerative process, not refractory depression.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. J is a 55-year-old clinical social worker with HIV (undetectable viral load on Biktarvy for 8 years), hypertension, and depression who is referred from her psychiatrist for neurological evaluation. She presents with her close friend of 20 years, who serves as the primary informant. Her psychiatrist referred her after 18 months of progressive behavioral and personality changes that have not responded to two antidepressant trials (escitalopram and now sertraline at 150 mg). Her friend describes a 15-month history of progressive behavioral changes that are markedly different from her previously known depressive episodes. She has become impulsive — she gave away her laptop to a stranger on the street, claiming he 'needed it more.' She made sexually inappropriate comments to a colleague at work, leading to an HR complaint, which she dismissed entirely. She now follows a rigid daily schedule of her own design and becomes agitated when anything deviates from it. She has developed a habit of watching the same nature documentary series every evening, having watched each episode more than 30 times. She shows no empathy toward clients, which her supervisor noted in an incident report — she was asking detailed questions about clients' trauma histories in front of other staff. She is on medical leave from work. She has no insight into these changes. Her HIV is well-controlled with Biktarvy — CD4 count 680 cells/uL, viral load undetectable for the past 6 years. She presents with a frontally predominant behavioral syndrome (disinhibition, compulsive behavior, loss of empathy, stereotypy) and inadequate response to antidepressants in her mid-50s.
